feat(api/addons): only reinstall addons when necessary

we now cache the `glide.addons.install_from_url` calls so that if the
given XPI URL has not changed, then we'll skip reinstalling the addon.

this handles cases where the addon has been updated in Glide directly,
and the XPI URL no longer directly matches the version of the installed
addon. this is intentional, as I'm going to also rename this method to
make the functionality more clear that you're just "requesting" that the
addon corresponding to the given XPI URL has been installed - it's not a
lock file.

more reasoning here is that it should be very rare that you actually
want to use an older version of an extension.

we may introduce an actual addons lock file in the future, the glide API
call is not the right place to do so, as it is user-controlled.

feat(internal): store last used version in the profile directory

Firefox currently only stores the last used version in a
compatability.ini file, but that is written to very early in startup so
we can't refference that in our code as it'll just be the same as the
current version.

So this patch ensures we write a
`glide__compatibility_oldest_version.txt` file the first time Gide is
launched, so that we can actually reference the previously installed
version.

Note this is redundant with `.glide/versions.json` but we still need it
for any breaking changes made after 0.1.53a, as that file won't be
available.

feat(scrolling): switch to smooth scrolling by default + increase compat

We now treat:
- `hjkl` as just normal arrow keys
- `<c-u>`/`<c-d>` as `<pageup>`/`<pagedown>`
- `G` as `<D-down>`/`<C-end>` on macos/linux
- `gg` as `<D-up>`/`<C-home>` on macos/linux

This change was made for a couple reasons:
1. we get a great smooth scrolling implementation for free, as Firefox's
   default for arrow keys is smooth scrolling.
2. just sending arrow keys increases compatibility, the previous
   implementation was very buggy, and would straight up not work in some
   cases, e.g. PDFs, or just stop working randomly

This is not a free lunch change though, as we're now sending arrow keys
to the content frame for hjkl, there are some implications, both good
and bad.

It's good because a website could have custom behaviour for arrow keys
that is more desirable than trying to scroll the frame.

It's also bad for the same reason, a user could reasonably be surprised
that hjkl no longer scrolls on a particular website they're using.

I think the trade off here is worth it for the increased compatibility
and smooth scrolling. We can revisit this in the future if it is indeed
problematic.

I also did *try* to figure out if it'd be possible to just call the
internal Firefox functions that pressing arrow keys ends up calling, but
that posed to be quite difficult. All of that logic is entrenched
heavily with the expectation that there is a KeyboardEvent. Additionally
attempting to just call the deeper internals, just resulted in the same
bugs that the current implementation has.

I wouldn't be surprised if there *is* a better way to do this, but I
don't think it's worth more time investment here trying to figure that
out.

feat(hints): add numeric label generator helper

The function is only a few lines, but we can help out users by providing
a stock implementation. Note that we ignore hint_chars here!

You might think that we could provide just a "sequential" generator that
would turn an alphabet like "abc" into:

  a, b, c, aa, ab, ac, ba, bb, bc, ca, cb, cc, aaa, ...

and then feed it the numeric digits via hint_chars. But that is not
quite how numbers work. If the alphabet is "1234567890", then we get "0"
instead of "10" as the tenth label, and "10" as the twentieth. If you
instead use "0123456789", then we start with "0" and get "01", "02",
etc, instead of the teens. You'd have to be smart about how zeroes are
handled, at which point it is easier to just have a custom generator
that simply counts.

feat(hints): accept <CR> to complete hint

With the default prefix-free hint labels, you never need to tell Glide
that you're done typing a hint. You just keep going until you complete a
hint or press a key which causes your sequence not to match any hint (in
which case we leave hint mode).

But for an arbitrary hint generator (including the numeric one), you
might end up with hints "1", "12", and "123". If you want hint "1", you
need some way to tell Glide that you're done, and it should look for
that string as a hint.

Let's teach the hint input handler to accept <CR> as a signal that we
should process the input we've gotten so far as a complete hint. This
lets the sequence (1, <CR>) find hint "1", while (1, 2, <CR>) will find
"12". A unique sequence like (1, 2, 3) will still yield hint "123"
without hitting <CR>. Likewise any key besides <CR> will still leave
hint mode. So (1, 2, <Space>) for example will behave as before.

fix(extensions/api): properly serialise browser.contentScripts.register() (#186)

previously if you called `browser.contentScripts.register()` you'd get an error about a value that couldn't be cloned. this happened because it returned an object like `{ unregister() { ... } }` and functions cannot be cloned.

now we strip `unregister()` before cloning it, and add `$glide_content_functions` to the result object so that the main process knows that there was a function defined in the content process, which it will then add back in, and forward any calls back to the content process.
